        "claim_label": "p2e:prop:bm-supported-trace-boundary",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Bose--Mesner supported trace and natural-action boundary]\n\\label{p2e:prop:bm-supported-trace-boundary}\nPaper~I-A, Theorem~\\ref{p1:thm:s3one-numerical-data}, provides the orthogonal\ncommon-space decomposition~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}\n\\[\n \\mathbb C^{2T}\n =\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}\\oplus\\mathcal E_9^{\\rm BM}.\n\\]\nFor the inclusion\n\\(\\iota_{15}:\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}\\hookrightarrow\\mathbb C^{2T}\\),\ndefine, without suppressing their carriers,\n\\[\n \\tau_{24}(A):=\\frac1{24}\\Tr_{\\mathbb C^{2T}}A,\n \\qquad\n \\tau_{15}(B):=\\frac1{15}\\Tr_{\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}}B.\n\\]\nThese normalized traces satisfy the equivalent identities\n\\[\n \\tau_{24}\\!\\left(\\iota_{15}B\\iota_{15}^*\\right)\n =\\frac{15}{24}\\,\\tau_{15}(B),\n \\qquad\n \\tau_{15}(B)\n =\\frac{24}{15}\\,\n  \\tau_{24}\\!\\left(\\iota_{15}B\\iota_{15}^*\\right),\n \\qquad\n B\\in\\End(\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}).\n\\]\nFor the natural left-\\(2T\\) actions used in Paper~I-A, there is no equivariant\nisomorphism\n\\[\n        \\mathcal H_1\\cong\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}.\n\\]\nNo such restriction is asserted for arbitrary vector-space isomorphisms or\nfor actions transported through a separately chosen isomorphism.\nThe natural-action statement is precisely Paper~I-A,\nProposition~\\ref{p1:prop:h1-e15-left-2t-obstruction}.\n\\end{proposition}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nBecause \\(\\iota_{15}\\) is an isometric inclusion,\n\\[\n \\Tr_{\\mathbb C^{2T}}(\\iota_{15}B\\iota_{15}^*)\n =\\Tr_{\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}}B.\n\\]\nDividing the left side by \\(24\\) and the right side by \\(15\\) proves the\nfirst trace identity; algebraic inversion proves the second.  The natural\nleft-\\(2T\\) equivariance obstruction is proved separately in\nPaper~II-F, Section~\\ref{p2e:app:natural-action-no-go}.\n\\end{proof}",

        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Empty natural-\\(2T\\) module-identification locus]\n\\label{p2e:cor:empty-natural-2t-identification-locus}\nThe two natural \\(2T\\)-modules \\(\\mathcal H_1\\) and\n\\(\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}\\) are separately admissible and both have complex\ndimension \\(15\\).  Their natural fixed subspaces, however, have dimensions\n\\[\n \\dim\\mathcal H_1^{2T}=6,\n \\qquad\n \\dim(\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM})^{2T}=1.\n\\]\nConsequently the joint locus obtained by adding a natural-\\(2T\\)-equivariant\nisomorphism relation is empty:\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\mathfrak Z_{\\rm nat\\text{-}iso}\n =\n \\operatorname{Iso}_{2T}^{\\rm nat}\n   (\\mathcal H_1,\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM})\n =\\varnothing.}\n\\]\nThe equality of total dimensions supplies ordinary vector-space isomorphisms\nbut no distinguished map and no natural equivariant one.  In the absence of\nthe isomorphism relation, the two differently typed modules may co-realize by\nrelation-free composition.  Transporting one action through a separately\nchosen vector-space isomorphism defines a different, map-dependent branch; it\ndoes not repair the empty natural-action locus.\n\\end{corollary}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nAn equivariant isomorphism maps invariant vectors bijectively to invariant\nvectors, so it would give an isomorphism between fixed subspaces and force\ntheir dimensions to agree.  Since \\(6\\neq1\\), no such map exists.  Ordinary\ndimension equality forgets the action, and transporting the action changes\nthe relation being tested, proving the remaining clauses.\n\\end{proof}",

          "An equivariant isomorphism restricts to a bijection of invariant spaces; 6≠1 refutes that relation. Equal total dimensions alone give only nondistinguished vector-space isomorphisms.",
          "Action transport through a chosen vector-space isomorphism changes the natural-action branch, so it is not a counterexample to emptiness."

        "source_lines": [
          1336,
          1363
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Kinematic cyclic trimer template]\n\\label{p2:prop:kinematic-cyclic-trimer-template}\nLet \\(T\\) be either oriented Paper-I-A trimer and let \\(X\\) be its\norientation-preserving cyclic shift.  Then \\(T\\) is a free transitive\n\\(Z_3\\)-set and\n\\[\n E_T:=\\mathbb C^T\\cong\\mathbb C[Z_3]\n \\cong\\mathbf1\\oplus\\chi\\oplus\\chi^{-1},\n \\qquad\n \\chi(X)=e^{2\\pi i/3}.\n\\]\nOn the underlying real permutation module,\n\\[\n        \\mathbb R^T\\cong\\mathbb R\\oplus W,\n        \\qquad\n        \\dim_{\\mathbb R}W=2,\n\\]\nand the pair module has\n\\[\n        \\dim_{\\mathbb C}(E_T\\otimes E_T^*)=9.\n\\]\n\\end{proposition}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1359,
          "end_line": 1363,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThese are the regular-representation and trimer-pair support statements of\nPaper~I-A, Theorem~\\ref{p1:thm:cyclic-trimer-operator-grammar}\n\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "type_signature": "Complex regular Z3 trimer module, real standard plane and pair module",
        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "Either oriented Paper-I-A trimer with orientation-preserving cyclic shift",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B2-RG-0040",
        "replay_steps": [
          "An oriented trimer has exactly three vertices; its orientation-preserving shift X has one orbit of length three, hence the Z3 action is free and transitive.",
          "Its complex permutation module is the regular representation of Z3. Discrete Fourier vectors furnish the trivial, chi, and inverse-chi lines. Reversing basis convention can exchange the latter two without changing the direct sum.",
          "Over the reals the constant vector spans R; its orthogonal sum-zero subspace W has real dimension two and carries the 120-degree rotation.",
          "The complex trimer-pair module E_T tensor E_T^* has dimension 3 times 3 = 9."
        ],

        "source_file": "Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex",
        "source_lines": [
          1365,
          1399
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[First-order Hermitian trimer grammar]\n\\label{p2:thm:primitive-trimer-grammar}\nIn a cyclic vertex basis, define\n\\[\n\\DtriI=\\operatorname{diag}\\!\\left(\\frac23,-\\frac13,-\\frac13\\right),\n\\qquad\n\\DtriII=\\operatorname{diag}(0,1,-1),\n\\]\n\\[\n C_1=X+X^\\dagger,\n \\qquad\n C_2=-i(X-X^\\dagger).\n\\]\nThe first-order Hermitian slice is\n\\[\n\\mathfrak T_{\\rm tri}\n=\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb R}\n\\{I,\\DtriI,\\DtriII,C_1,C_2\\}.\n\\]\nEquivalently, every element of the slice has the form\n\\[\n H=\\alpha I+\\beta\\DtriI+\\gamma\\DtriII+\\rho C(\\phi),\n \\qquad\n C(\\phi)=e^{-i\\phi}X+e^{i\\phi}X^2,\n\\]\nwith\n\\(\\alpha,\\beta,\\gamma\\in\\mathbb R\\),\n\\(\\rho\\ge0\\), and\n\\(\\phi\\in\\mathbb R/(2\\pi\\mathbb Z)\\).\n\\end{theorem}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1396,
          "end_line": 1399,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThis is Paper~I-A, Theorem~\\ref{p1:thm:cyclic-trimer-operator-grammar}, restated\nin Paper-II notation~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "type_signature": "Five-dimensional first-order Hermitian trimer slice",
        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "Cyclic vertex basis; X cyclic shift; alpha,beta,gamma real; rho>=0; phi modulo 2pi",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B2-RG-0041",
        "replay_steps": [
          "Since X^3=I and X is a unitary permutation, X^dagger=X^2. C1=X+X^dagger and C2=-i(X-X^dagger) are Hermitian.",
          "The three real diagonal Hermitian directions are spanned by I, DtriI, DtriII, with DtriI and DtriII independent trace-zero diagonals.",
          "C1 and C2 are independent off-diagonal Hermitian directions; their support is disjoint from the diagonal subspace, giving real dimension five.",
          "For aC1+bC2 choose rho=sqrt(a^2+b^2) and phi with a=rho cos(phi), b=rho sin(phi). Then rho C(phi)=rho(e^(-i phi)X+e^(i phi)X^2). At rho=0 arbitrary phi represents the same zero vector, and the target asserts existence only.",
          "This is the first-order slice retaining one cyclic transport orbit, as explicitly defined in I-A; it is not asserted to be the full Hermitian algebra or a physical closure algebra."
        ],
        "consumed_imports": [
          "p1:thm:cyclic-trimer-operator-grammar"
        ],
        "condition_predicates_for_canonical_match": [
          "Cyclic trimer vertex basis",
          "alpha,beta,gamma real; rho>=0; phi modulo 2pi"
        ],

        "candidate_issues": [],
        "E3_claimed": false,
        "source_label": "p2:thm:primitive-trimer-grammar",
        "evidence_level": "E1",
        "import_records": [

        "source_file": "Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex",
        "source_lines": [
          1401,
          1435
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Kinematic trimer Weyl and \\(A_2\\) defect constants]\n\\label{p2:cor:kinematic-trimer-weyl-a2}\nLet \\(\\omega=e^{2\\pi i/3}\\), \\(Ze_j=\\omega^je_j\\), and\n\\(Xe_j=e_{j+1}\\).  Then\n\\[\n X^3=Z^3=I,\n \\qquad\n ZX=\\omega XZ,\n\\]\nand the nine operators \\(X^aZ^b\\), \\(a,b\\in\\mathbb Z_3\\), form a\ntrace-orthogonal basis of \\(M_3(\\mathbb C)\\).  For\n\\(D_j=P_j-I/3\\),\n\\[\n \\operatorname{tr}(D_j^2)=\\frac23,\n \\qquad\n \\operatorname{tr}(D_iD_j)=-\\frac13\n \\quad(i\\ne j).\n\\]\nFor \\(\\alpha_1=P_0-P_1\\) and \\(\\alpha_2=P_1-P_2\\),\n\\[\n\\operatorname{tr}(\\alpha_i\\alpha_j)\n=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n2&-1\\\\\n-1&2\n\\end{pmatrix}_{ij}.\n\\]\nThus the resulting defect plane is the \\(A_2\\) root/weight plane.\n\\end{corollary}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1431,
          "end_line": 1435,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThese are the Paper-I-A finite Weyl and trimer-defect identities following from\nTheorem~\\ref{p1:thm:cyclic-trimer-operator-grammar}\n\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "type_signature": "Finite Weyl basis and trace-metric A2 defect plane",
        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "X e_j=e_(j+1); Z e_j=omega^j e_j; indices mod3",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B2-RG-0042",
        "replay_steps": [
          "On e_j, ZX e_j=omega^(j+1)e_(j+1)=omega XZ e_j. The order-three identities follow from the periodic basis and omega^3=1.",
          "For W_ab=X^a Z^b, tr(W_ab^dagger W_cd)=3 delta_(a,c) delta_(b,d): if shifts differ there are no diagonal entries; if shifts agree, the trace is the finite Fourier sum. Thus the nine operators are a Hilbert-Schmidt trace-orthogonal basis of M3(C).",
          "With tr(P_iP_j)=delta_ij and tr(I)=3, tr((P_j-I/3)^2)=1-2/3+1/3=2/3, and for i!=j the cross trace is 0-1/3-1/3+1/3=-1/3.",
          "For alpha1=P0-P1 and alpha2=P1-P2 the diagonal norms are 2 and cross inner product is -1, exactly the printed A2 Cartan Gram matrix.",
          "The roots and centered projectors lie in the same real trace-zero diagonal plane; the root/weight-plane descriptor does not identify their different integral lattices."
        ],
        "consumed_imports": [

        ],

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Imported Paper-I-A protected commutant]\n\\label{p2:prop:kin-u1-commutant}\nPaper~I-A, Theorem~\\ref{p1:thm:s3one-commutant-line}, proves that the\ncomplex-linear commutant and its Hermitian part are~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}\n\\[\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})\n=\\mathbb CP_L\\oplus\\mathbb CP_R\n=\\mathbb CI_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}\\oplus\\mathbb C\\Gamma_{\\rm sp},\n\\]\n\\[\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}\n=\\mathbb RP_L\\oplus\\mathbb RP_R\n=\\mathbb RI_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}\\oplus\\mathbb R\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}.\n\\]\nPaper~II-E uses this as an imported theorem and does not re-prove the Schur\ndecomposition.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "source_proof": null,
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",

        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "Multiplicity-one inequivalent two-dimensional left/right irreducibles",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B2-RG-0047",
        "replay_steps": [
          "The two protected summands are inequivalent irreducible complex Spin(4) modules. Schur gives one complex scalar on each and no off-diagonal intertwiner.",
          "Thus End_Spin4(S_prot)=C P_L direct sum C P_R=C I direct sum C Gamma_sp.",
          "P_L and P_R are orthogonal Hermitian projectors. A block scalar is self-adjoint precisely when both scalar coefficients are real, proving the stated Hermitian part.",
          "Complex linearity is essential to the target domain; possible real-linear quaternionic or antiunitary structures do not enlarge this declared commutant."
        ],

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Finite antipodal lifts on the protected block]\n\\label{p2e:cor:protected-antipodal-lifts}\nLet\n\\[\n z_L=(-I,I),\\qquad z_R=(I,-I),\\qquad z_c=(-I,-I)\n\\]\nas in Paper~II-D.  On\n\\(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}=V_{\\frac12,0}\\oplus V_{0,\\frac12}\\),\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\rho(z_L)=-\\Gamma_{\\rm sp},\\qquad\n        \\rho(z_R)=+\\Gamma_{\\rm sp},\\qquad\n        \\rho(z_c)=-I_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}.}\n\\]\nThus a provenance-fixed Hopf half-turn may coincide, up to the inherited\nhanded sign, with the protected grading as a finite involution.  This does not\nidentify the infinitesimal Hopf generator with \\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\) and does\nnot select a nonzero gauged abelian generator.\n\\end{corollary}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1523,
          "end_line": 1528,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nOn \\(V_{\\frac12,0}\\), \\(z_L\\) acts by \\(-1\\) and \\(z_R\\) by \\(+1\\); on\n\\(V_{0,\\frac12}\\) the signs are reversed.  Writing the resulting diagonal\noperators in terms of \\(P_L,P_R\\) gives the first two identities, and their\nproduct gives the third.\n\\end{proof}"
        },

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{remark}[Marked versus unmarked round symmetry]\n\\label{p2e:rem:marked-hopf-symmetry}\nThe unmarked round parent retains the full connected round symmetry\n\\(\\Spin(4)\\).  Fixing one oriented Hopf representative is additional\nconstituted data; its connected geometric stabilizer is the corresponding\n\\(U(2)\\)-type subgroup (equivalently, at spin-cover level, one full chiral\n\\(SU(2)\\) together with the selected Cartan \\(U(1)\\) in the opposite factor,\nwith the standard central quotient).  This reduced stabilizer belongs to one\nmarked representative.  The family obtained by conjugating that representative\nwith already generated round isometries is still \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-covariant.\n\\end{remark}",
        "source_proof": null,

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Oriented-Hopf marked commutants]\n\\label{p2e:thm:oriented-hopf-marked-commutants}\nFix one oriented left-fibre Hopf representative, with the conventions of\nPaper~II-D, Definition~\\ref{p2:def:finite-diagonal-spin-weight-hopf-charge},\nand put \\(Q_H:=Q_{H,L}=-2L_3^-\\).  At spin-cover level its stabilizer is\n\\(K_H=SU(2)_L\\times U(1)_R\\), and the protected restriction is\n\\[\n \\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}|_{K_H}\n =(\\mathbf2)_0\\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{+1}\\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{-1}.\n\\]\nLet \\(P_R^{(\\pm)}\\) project onto the \\(Q_H=\\pm1\\) right-handed\neigenlines, so \\(P_R=P_R^{(+)}+P_R^{(-)}\\).  Then\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\End_{K_H}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})\n =\\mathbb CP_L\\oplus\\mathbb CP_R^{(+)}\\oplus\\mathbb CP_R^{(-)}\n \\cong\\mathbb C^3,}\n\\]\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\End_{K_H}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\rm sa}_0\n =\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb R}\\{\\Gamma_{\\rm sp},Q_H\\},\\qquad\n Q_H^2=P_R,\\qquad\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}=I-2Q_H^2.}\n\\]\nFor the full level-one carrier the corresponding commutant is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\End_{K_H}(\\mathcal H_1)\\cong\n M_2(\\mathbb C)\\oplus\\mathbb C^8.}\n\\]\nThese are pointwise commutants for the marked symmetry action, not\ncommutants of a covariant derivative.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1573,
          "end_line": 1594,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThe three protected summands displayed above are inequivalent irreducible\n\\(K_H\\)-modules, so Schur's lemma gives their three scalar blocks.\nThe first has dimension two and the last two have dimension one.\nConsequently \\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\) and \\(Q_H\\) span the two-dimensional\ntraceless Hermitian part.  The eigenvalues \\(0,+1,-1\\) give the two\npolynomial identities.\n\nRestricting the six summands of Paper~II-D,\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:diagonal-center-grading}, gives\n\\[\n \\mathcal H_1|_{K_H}\n =2(\\mathbf1)_0\\oplus(\\mathbf2)_0\n \\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{+1}\\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{-1}\n \\oplus(\\mathbf2)_{+1}\\oplus(\\mathbf2)_{-1}\n \\oplus(\\mathbf3)_0\n \\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{+2}\\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{-2}.\n\\]\nThe two copies of \\((\\mathbf1)_0\\) come from \\(V_{0,0}\\) and the\nzero Hopf weight of \\(V_{0,1}\\).  All eight other types occur once.\nSchur's lemma therefore gives \\(M_2(\\mathbb C)\\oplus\\mathbb C^8\\).\n\\end{proof}"

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Traceless refinement of the imported commutant]\n\\label{p2:thm:kin-u1-unique}\nDefine\n\\[\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}_0\n:=\n\\{Q\\in\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}:\n       \\Tr_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}Q=0\\}.\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}_0\n=\\mathbb R\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}.\n\\]\nThe quotient map restricts to an isomorphism\n\\[\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}_0\n\\xrightarrow{\\ \\cong\\ }\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}/\n\\mathbb RI_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}},\n\\qquad\nq_{\\rm prot}\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\n\\longmapsto[q_{\\rm prot}\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}].\n\\]\nThus every quotient class has the unique traceless representative\n\\(q_{\\rm prot}\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\). Since both summands have\ndimension \\(2\\),\n\\[\n        \\Tr_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}Q=2(a+b).\n\\]\nTracelessness gives \\(b=-a\\), hence\n\\(Q=a(P_L-P_R)=a\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\).  The quotient statement is the\nsame calculation without choosing a traceless representative.\n\\end{proof}",

          1731,

        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Explicit protected-block grading-weighted traces]\n\\label{p2:prop:protected-anomaly-traces}\nFor \\(Q=aP_L+bP_R\\),\n\\[\n        \\mathcal A_1(Q)=2(a-b),\n        \\qquad\n        \\mathcal A_3(Q)=2(a^3-b^3).\n\\]\nIn particular, for the traceless non-scalar line\n\\(Q=q_{\\rm prot}\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\),\n\\[\n        \\mathcal A_1(q_{\\rm prot}\\Gamma_{\\rm sp})=4q_{\\rm prot},\n        \\qquad\n        \\mathcal A_3(q_{\\rm prot}\\Gamma_{\\rm sp})\n        =4q_{\\rm prot}^{\\,3}.\n\\]\n\nThe factor \\(2\\) in both coefficients is\n\\(\\rank P_L=\\dim V_{(1/2,0)}=2\\), the complex chiral-spinor dimension of each\nprotected summand.  It is therefore a spinor trace multiplicity at this stage,\nnot a Weyl-species count.  Only after a later Lorentzian Weyl interpretation\nis supplied does the same factor become a Lorentz-spin trace normalization.  A species-normalized anomaly\ncoefficient counts one unit per Weyl species and would read \\(a-b\\) and\n\\(a^3-b^3\\).  The two normalizations cannot be reconciled by rescaling the\ncharge, since \\(Q\\mapsto\\lambda Q\\) sends \\(\\mathcal A_1\\mapsto\\lambda\\mathcal\nA_1\\) but \\(\\mathcal A_3\\mapsto\\lambda^3\\mathcal A_3\\).  The common zero locus\nis unaffected, so the no-go statement below is independent of the choice.\n\\end{proposition}",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "scope": "All real a,b in Q=aP_L+bP_R, protected spinor trace of rank2+2 blocks.",
        "proof_source_lines": [
          1760,
          1774
        ],
        "proof_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nUse\n\\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}P_L=P_L\\),\n\\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}P_R=-P_R\\),\n\\(\\Tr P_L=\\Tr P_R=2\\), and\n\\(P_LP_R=0\\).  Then\n\\[\n\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}Q=aP_L-bP_R,\n\\qquad\n\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}Q^3=a^3P_L-b^3P_R,\n\\]\nwhich gives the formulas.  Substituting\n\\(a=q_{\\rm prot}\\) and \\(b=-q_{\\rm prot}\\) gives the\nlast pair.\n\\end{proof}",

        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Protected-block trace kernel and chirality-distinguishing no-go]\n\\label{p2:thm:protected-anomaly-no-go}\nAmong all Hermitian \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-equivariant generators \\(Q=aP_L+bP_R\\), the complete\ncommon kernel of the grading-weighted linear and cubic traces is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\ker\\mathcal A_1\\cap\\ker\\mathcal A_3\n =\\{aI_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}:a\\in\\mathbb R\\}.}\n\\]\nConsequently no chirality-distinguishing generator, equivalently no point with\n\\(a\\ne b\\), lies in the common kernel.  On the traceless commutant line the\nonly common-kernel point is zero.  The surviving scalar line is vector-like\nwith respect to \\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\) and is not excluded by this finite trace\ncalculation.\nConditional on the physical chirality and gauged-\\(U(1)\\) identifications\nstated above, this finite trace no-go becomes a perturbative anomaly\nobstruction to a protected-only chirality-distinguishing generator.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "scope": "All Hermitian Spin(4)-equivariant Q=aP_L+bP_R on protected block; physical perturbative obstruction only under declared interpretation.",
        "proof_source_lines": [
          1804,
          1811
        ],
        "proof_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nProposition~\\ref{p2:prop:protected-anomaly-traces} gives\n\\(\\mathcal A_1(Q)=2(a-b)\\).  Hence\n\\(\\mathcal A_1(Q)=0\\) implies \\(a=b\\), and then \\(Q=aI_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}\\);\nthe cubic trace also vanishes.  If \\(Q\\) is traceless, then\n\\(2(a+b)=4a=0\\), so \\(Q=0\\).  Equivalently, on the traceless line the\ndisplayed grading-weighted traces vanish only for \\(q_{\\rm prot}=0\\).\n\\end{proof}",

        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Protected trace-free and chirality-distinguishing joint loci]\n\\label{p2e:cor:protected-anomaly-free-joint-locus}\nOn the full Hermitian \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-equivariant commutant, the joint zero locus is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\mathfrak Z_{\\rm eq}\n =\\{(a,b)\\in\\mathbb R^2:\n      2(a-b)=0,\\ 2(a^3-b^3)=0\\}\n =\\{(t,t):t\\in\\mathbb R\\}.}\n\\]\nIts intersection with the chirality-distinguishing stratum is empty:\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\mathfrak Z_{\\rm eq}\\cap\\{(a,b):a\\ne b\\}=\\varnothing.}\n\\]\nOn the protected traceless commutant line, the same classification reduces to\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\mathfrak Z_{\\rm tr}\n =\\{q_{\\rm prot}\\in\\mathbb R:\n     4q_{\\rm prot}=0,\\ 4q_{\\rm prot}^{\\,3}=0\\}\n =\\{0\\}.}\n\\]\nTherefore adjoining an independently required nonzero traceless protected\ngenerator gives the empty joint locus\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\mathfrak Z_{\\rm tr}\\cap\n        \\{q_{\\rm prot}\\neq0\\}=\\varnothing.}\n\\]\nUnder the physical anomaly interpretation stated above, there is no\nprotected-only anomaly-free \\(U(1)\\) whose generator distinguishes the two\nchiral constituents.  A scalar vector-like \\(U(1)\\) is not ruled out by these\ntwo traces.  GP3 cannot select around the empty chirality-distinguishing locus.\n\nIf additional chiral matter sectors occur, cancellation is a new joint\nfibre-product problem.  Writing their contributions as\n\\((B_1,B_3)\\), the required equations are\n\\[\n 4q_{\\rm prot}+B_1=0,\n \\qquad\n 4q_{\\rm prot}^{\\,3}+B_3=0.\n\\]\nNeither the existence of extra sectors nor either equation is generated by\nthe protected-block calculation.\n\\end{corollary}",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "scope": "Joint real charge loci on the full commutant and its traceless line; enlarged matter contributions only on an independently supplied actual representation.",
        "proof_source_lines": [
          1858,
          1865
        ],
        "proof_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe theorem above gives the scalar common kernel in the full commutant and its\nsingleton traceless representative.  Intersecting the scalar kernel with\n\\(a\\ne b\\), or the traceless singleton with the nonzero stratum, is empty.\nTrace additivity gives the two displayed equations for an enlarged matter\nrepresentation, which must be solved on that representation's actual typed\ncharge atlas.\n\\end{proof}",
        "replay_steps": [
          "The previous theorem gives Z_eq={(t,t)} and its intersection with a≠b is empty.",

        "statement_source_lines": [
          1867,
          1892
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Oriented-Hopf protected weighted trace-zero locus]\n\\label{p2e:thm:marked-hopf-weighted-trace-locus}\nOn the marked domain of\nTheorem~\\ref{p2e:thm:oriented-hopf-marked-commutants}, write\n\\[\n T=aP_L+b_+P_R^{(+)}+b_-P_R^{(-)},\\qquad a,b_+,b_-\\in\\mathbb R.\n\\]\nFor the same grading-weighted functionals\n\\(\\mathcal A_k(T)=\\Tr(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}T^k)\\), \\(k=1,3\\), one has\n\\[\n \\mathcal A_1(T)=2a-b_+-b_-,\\qquad\n \\mathcal A_3(T)=2a^3-b_+^3-b_-^3,\n\\]\nand the exact common zero locus is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\{T:\\mathcal A_1(T)=\\mathcal A_3(T)=0\\}\n =\\mathbb RI\\ \\cup\\ \\mathbb RQ_H.}\n\\]\nIts ordinary-traceless part is exactly \\(\\mathbb RQ_H\\).\nThis is a union of two lines, not their linear span.\nIt changes the invariance group of\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:protected-anomaly-no-go} and therefore leaves that\nunmarked theorem intact.  The spacetime-chirality and internal-charge\nidentifications required for a physical anomaly interpretation remain\nseparate; splitting geometric magnetic weights does not supply them.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "scope": "Oriented-Hopf marked K_H commutant: ranks2,1,1 and real a,b+,b−.",
        "proof_source_lines": [
          1894,
          1902
        ],
        "proof_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe ranks of \\(P_L,P_R^{(+)},P_R^{(-)}\\) are \\(2,1,1\\), respectively,\nand \\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\) acts on them as \\(+1,-1,-1\\), proving the\ntrace formulas.  The first zero condition gives \\(b_\\pm=a\\pm d\\).\nSubstitution into the cubic gives \\(\\mathcal A_3=-6ad^2\\).  Over\n\\(\\mathbb R\\) the alternatives are \\(d=0\\), giving \\(T=aI\\), or\n\\(a=0\\), giving \\(T=dQ_H\\).  Their ordinary traces are \\(4a\\) and zero,\nso only \\(\\mathbb RQ_H\\) survives ordinary tracelessness.\n\\end{proof}",
        "replay_steps": [
          "The same Γ has eigenvalue+1 on rank2 left block and−1 on each rank1 right line, giving A1=2a−b+−b− and A3=2a³−b+³−b−³.",
          "A1=0 is equivalent to b+=a+d,b−=a−d for reald.",
          "Expand (a+d)³+(a−d)³=2a³+6ad², hence cubic residual−6ad².",
          "OverR, ad²=0 iff d=0 or a=0. The first branch is aI, the second dQ_H, so the common locus is RI ∪ RQ_H.",
          "On the locus ordinary trace is4a, so its traceless slice is exactlyRQ_H.",
          "The sum I+Q_H has a=d=1 and residual−6, showing why the union is not the linear span. Its changed invariance domain does not contradict the unmarked theorem."
        ],

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{lemma}[Valid odd-character trace identities]\n\\label{p2:lem:odd-character-trace}\nFor \\(Q=q_{\\rm prot}\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\) and every\n\\(n\\in\\mathbb Z_{\\ge0}\\),\n\\[\n        \\Tr_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}(Q^{2n+1})=0.\n\\]\nThese are ordinary character-trace identities.         "source_file": "Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex",
        "source_lines": [
          1967,
          1996
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Same-curvature line transfer is fixed by flat holonomy]\n\\label{p2e:thm:v2210-lit-line-holonomy}\nLet $L_1,L_2$ be Hermitian line bundles on the same connected base and\nlet $T:L_1\\to L_2$ be a specified unitary bundle isomorphism.  Transport\n$\\nabla_1$ by $T$ and suppose it and $\\nabla_2$ have the same curvature.\nThere is then a global real one-form $\\alpha$ such that\n\\[\n \\nabla_2-T\\nabla_1T^{-1}=i\\alpha,\\qquad \\mathrm d\\alpha=0.\n\\]\nFor every closed loop $\\gamma$,\n\\[\n \\frac{\\operatorname{Hol}_{\\nabla_2}(\\gamma)}\n {\\operatorname{Hol}_{T\\nabla_1T^{-1}}(\\gamma)}\n =\\exp\\left(-i\\oint_\\gamma\\alpha\\right).\n\\]\nThe two connections are gauge-equivalent exactly when all these ratios are\none, equivalently when every period of $\\alpha$ belongs to $2\\pi\\mathbb Z$.\nOn a simply connected base, equality of curvature after the specified\nbundle identification is sufficient.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1987,
          "end_line": 1996,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nDifferences of unitary line connections are imaginary scalar one-forms,\nand their curvature difference is $i\\mathrm d\\alpha$.  Parallel transport\nof the difference along a loop gives the exponential.  If all periods are\nintegral multiples of $2\\pi$, choose a base point and define the unitary\ngauge by $\\exp(-i\\int\\alpha)$; the period condition makes it independent\nof the path and it transports the first connection to the second.\nConversely a unitary gauge has integral $2\\pi$ periods and leaves loop\nholonomies equal.  On a simply connected base a closed one-form is exact.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "type_signature": "Unitary line connections with specified unitary bundle identification",
        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "Same connected smooth base; T given; equal transported curvatures",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B3-RG-0066",
        "evidence_level": "E1",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "replay_steps": [
          "The specified unitary isomorphism T places both connections on the same Hermitian line. Their difference is a globally defined imaginary scalar one-form i alpha.",
          "For line connections the curvature difference is i d alpha; equal curvature gives d alpha=0.",
          "The parallel-transport equation for the difference yields Hol2/Hol1=exp(-i integral_loop alpha), with the sign matching the declared connection difference.",
          "If every period is 2pi times an integer, g(x)=exp(-i integral_(x0 to x) alpha) is single-valued and satisfies g nabla1 g^-1=nabla1+i alpha=nabla2.",
          "Conversely a U1-valued gauge changes its phase by integer multiples of 2pi around loops, so all holonomy ratios are one. On a simply connected smooth base, a closed real one-form is exact."
        ],

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Equal degrees do not identify every native charge owner]\n\\label{p2e:cor:v2210-lit-degree-versus-phase}\nOn the actual Hopf base $S^2$, aligned orientation, the supplied line\nisomorphism and equal curvature suffice to identify the transported phase\nconnection up to gauge.  Equal Chern degree alone fixes neither the\ncurvature representative nor that isomorphism.  On $M_8$, even equal\ncurvature can leave a flat phase difference on its two scalar circles.\n\\end{corollary}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 2006,
          "end_line": 2012,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nApply the preceding theorem and $H^1(S^2;\\mathbb R)=0$.  The supplied\nproduct has $H_1(M_8;\\mathbb Z)=\\mathbb Z^2$; flat unitary differences\ncan therefore have independent holonomies on the two scalar generators.\nEquality of Chern degree concerns the integral curvature class, not a\npointwise curvature form or these flat holonomies.\n\\end{proof}"
        },

        "source_file": "Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex",
        "source_lines": [
          2089,
          2124
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Ten local $S_3$ trimer fibres and their $A_2$ tangent planes]\n\\label{p2e:thm:v318-local-petersen-trimer}\nOn an occurring $2I$ packet, every vertex of the Petersen graph is a\nthreefold Hopf-axis line $[u_{ij}]$.  Its $A_5$ setwise stabilizer has\norder six and is isomorphic to $S_3$; it permutes its three\nPetersen neighbors faithfully.  Its real permutation module splits\ncanonically as $\\mathbf1\\oplus W_{A_2}$, with\n\\[\n W_{A_2}=\\{(a,b,c)\\in\\mathbb R^3:a+b+c=0\\},\n \\qquad\\dim W_{A_2}=2.\n\\]\nWith a representative axis and compatible cyclic orientations, the\nPetersen cross-product directions $n_1,n_2,n_3\\in u_{ij}^{\\perp}$\nform an $A_2$ root trimer and the map\n$W_u=\\sqrt{2/3}\\,(n_1\\ n_2\\ n_3)$ satisfies\n\\[\n W_uW_u^{\\mathsf T}=I_3-u_{ij}u_{ij}^{\\mathsf T},\\qquad\n W_u^{\\mathsf T}W_u=I_3-\\tfrac13J_3.\n\\]\nThus the local trimer-defect plane is isometric to the transverse\nHopf/Clifford tangent plane, conditional on its labelled frame.\nThis is not an automatic identification with the earlier one-core\n$C_6^{\\rm link}$, its $\\mathbb C[Z_3]$ module, or the complex\nfundamental color representation.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 2114,
          "end_line": 2124,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThe stabilizer in $A_5$ of a two-label subset $\\{i,j\\}$ has\norder $60/10=6$; for every permutation of the three unused labels\nthere is a unique parity-compatible permutation of the selected pair.\nHence its action on the three unused two-label combinations is all\n$S_3$.  The permutation module decomposes into its constant\nline and its standard $A_2$ plane.  The transverse identities are\nthe exact vector-projector identities of Paper~I-A, and the map\nannihilates the constant line while preserving the inner product\non $W_{A_2}$.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",

        "evidence_id": "IIE-B3-RG-0073",

        "replay_steps": [

        "source_lines": [
          2126,
          2143
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[No global flat assignment of three edge colors]\n\\label{p2e:prop:v318-snark-no-flat-trimer}\nThe Petersen graph is not properly three-edge-colorable: its edge\nchromatic number is four.  Consequently its ten local three-channel\ntrimer fibres cannot all be identified with a single globally\nconstant three-color edge labelling.  This is a \\emph{flat labelling}\nobstruction, not a no-go theorem for a nontrivial local transition\nsystem, an $SU(3)$-valued color connection, or a physical color\nsinglet; each requires its own action/representation theorem.\n\\end{proposition}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 2136,
          "end_line": 2143,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nIn any three-edge-coloring of a cubic graph, one color is a\nperfect matching.  Every perfect matching of the Petersen graph\nhas as its complement two disjoint five-cycles.  The remaining\ntwo colors would have to alternate around each cycle, impossible\nbecause a five-cycle is odd.  A four-edge-coloring exists by the\nstandard degree-four edge-coloring of the Petersen graph.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",

        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "Proper flat global edge-colour assignment",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B3-RG-0074",

        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "replay_steps": [

          "The conclusion concerns a single globally constant flat edge-color label. It does not refute locally varying transition data, an SU3 connection, or a color-singlet contraction."

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Minimal exact-position protected-readout resource]\n\\label{p2e:cor:v266-minimal-protected-readout}\nFor the intrinsic finite tuple, a single exact-position POVM with five\noutcomes has effect span exactly\n$\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb R}\\{I,X_1^D,\\ldots,X_4^D\\}$ and is blind to\nboth the protected population $P_S$ and protected chirality\n$\\widetilde\\chi=P_S\\chi$. For $r\\ge2\\Rmom$, six native outcomes suffice\nand are necessary to add \\emph{either} observable directly to the four\ncoordinate moments, while seven are sufficient and necessary to add\n\\emph{both} independently. A generic native single-setting\ninformationally complete frame still requires $137$ outcomes, and can\ncarry exact moments only at $r>\\sqrt3\\Rmom$.\n\\end{corollary}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 2275,
          "end_line": 2282,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThe five/six/seven direct-effect systems and their lower bounds are\nTheorem~\\ref{p2c:thm:v266-minimal-protected-readout}; the complete\nframe condition is\nTheorem~\\ref{p2c:thm:v258-minimal-complete-readout}.\nThe fact that $P_S$ and $\\widetilde\\chi$ are coordinate-polynomial\noperators does not make them linear combinations of five POVM effects.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",

        "replay_steps": [
          "Five effects with exact I,X1,...,X4 constraints span a five-dimensional effect system because the five moment operators are independent. The affine coefficient matrix is invertible, so every effect lies in their span, giving equality.",

          "For r>=2R the source supplies six effects using two orthogonal trines with an independent contrast proportional to either P_S or protected chirality, while preserving all four exact coordinate moments and positivity.",
          "A seven-effect construction uses two independent scalar/vector-null contrasts to recover both P_S and protected chirality. Seven target operators are linearly independent; the corresponding six-target independence proves the minimal six-effect count for either alone.",
          "For full native informational completeness the real Hermitian dimension is 11^2+4^2=137, and fewer effects cannot separate all native states.         "source_excerpt": "\n\\begin{definition}[\\texorpdfstring{\\(S^3_1\\)}{S3_1} skeleton and coordinate-completion family]\n\\label{p1:def:s3one-finite-geometry-datum}\nThe derived level-one skeleton is\n\\[\n    \\mathsf B_{\\rm skel}\n    =\n    (S^3(\\Rmom),\\mathcal H_\\bullet,\\mathcal H_1),\n\\]\nwhere \\(\\mathcal H_\\bullet=\\{\\mathcal H_m\\}_{m\\ge0}\\) is the integer-level\nfinite \\(\\operatorname{Sp}in(4)\\)-equivariant module family.  Let\n\\(\\mathfrak M_{\\rm coord}(\\mathcal H_1)\\) be the family of Hermitian\n\\(\\operatorname{Sp}in(4)\\)-equivariant vector quadruples on \\(\\mathcal H_1\\) that match the\nnormalized scalar multiplication edge.  Corollary~\\ref{p1:cor:level-one-coordinate-completion-moduli}\nproves that, after quotienting by sector rephasings, the four-edge forest\nleaves exactly three nonnegative reduced magnitudes:\n\\[\n \\mathfrak M_{\\rm coord}(\\mathcal H_1)/{\\sim}\n \\;\\cong\\;\n \\mathbb R_{\\ge0}^{3},\n \\qquad\n [\\mathsf C]\\longleftrightarrow\n (r_{1,0},r_{0,1},\\varrho_{\\rm sp}).\n\\]\nHere the first two entries are the two geometric off-diagonal magnitudes and\n\\(\\varrho_{\\rm sp}\\) is the phase-invariant protected magnitude.  Frames,\nbases, and removable edge phases are presentation conventions.\n\nFor every completion class define its protected radius\n\\[\n \\rho_{\\mathsf C}:=2\\varrho_{\\rm sp}(\\mathsf C)\\ge0.\n\\]"
      }

        ],
        "source_excerpt": "\\label{p1:prop:general-protected-clifford-relation}\nLet \\(\\mathsf C\\in\\mathfrak M_{\\rm coord}(\\mathcal H_1)\\) be arbitrary and\nwrite\n\\[\n X_a:=\\widehat X_{a,\\mathcal K}^{\\mathsf B},\n \\qquad\n \\rho_{\\mathsf C}:=2\\varrho_{\\rm sp}\\ge0.\n\\]\nWith the reduced-magnitude convention\n\\[\n \\sum_{a=1}^4X_a^2=4\\varrho_{\\rm sp}^{\\,2}\\mathbf1_{\\mathcal K}\n =\\rho_{\\mathsf C}^{\\,2}\\mathbf1_{\\mathcal K},\n\\]\nthe protected coordinates satisfy on the full cone\n\\[\n \\{X_a,X_b\\}\n =2\\varrho_{\\rm sp}^{\\,2}\\delta_{ab}\\mathbf1_{\\mathcal K}\n =\\frac{\\rho_{\\mathsf C}^{\\,2}}2\\delta_{ab}\\mathbf1_{\\mathcal K}.\n\\]\nIf \\(\\rho_{\\mathsf C}=0\\), Hermiticity forces \\(X_a=0\\) for all \\(a\\).\nIf \\(\\rho_{\\mathsf C}>0\\), the normalized operators\n\\[\n \\Gamma_a^{\\mathsf C}:=\\frac{2}{\\rho_{\\mathsf C}}X_a\n\\]\nobey\n\\(\\{\\Gamma_a^{\\mathsf C},\\Gamma_b^{\\mathsf C}\\}\n=2\\delta_{ab}\\mathbf1_{\\mathcal K}\\).  Thus inverse-normalized gamma,"

        "source_excerpt": "\\]\nFor a unital star algebra, this compression preserves multiplication\nexactly if and only if $P$ reduces the algebra.\n\\end{lemma}\n\\begin{proof}\nInsert $ZZ^\\dagger=P$ between the two compressed factors. If the defect\nvanishes, take $B=A^\\dagger$: the positive matrix\n$Z^\\dagger A(I-P)A^\\dagger Z$ vanishes, so\n$(I-P)A^\\dagger Z=0$. Applying this to every $A$ and its adjoint proves\nreduction. The converse follows from $[P,A]=0$."

      "source_as_printed": "and put \\(Q_H:=Q_{H,L}=-2L_3^-\\).       "source_as_printed": " \\boxed{\\End_{K_H}(\\mathcal H_1)\\cong\n M_2(\\mathbb C)\\oplus\\mathbb C^8.}\n\\]\nThese are pointwise commutants for the marked symmetry action, not\ncommutants of a covariant derivative.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe three protected summands displayed above are inequivalent irreducible\n\\(K_H\\)-modules, so Schur's lemma gives their three scalar blocks.\nThe first has dimension two and the last two have dimension one.\nConsequently \\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\) and \\(Q_H\\) span the two-dimensional\ntraceless Hermitian part.  The eigenvalues \\(0,+1,-1\\) give the two\npolynomial identities.\n\nRestricting the six summands of Paper~II-D,\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:diagonal-center-grading}, gives\n\\[\n \\mathcal H_1|_{K_H}\n =2(\\mathbf1)_0\\oplus(\\mathbf2)_0\n \\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{+1}\\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{-1}\n \\oplus(\\mathbf2)_{+1}\\oplus(\\mathbf2)_{-1}\n \\oplus(\\mathbf3)_0\n \\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{+2}\\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{-2}.\n\\]\nThe two copies of \\((\\mathbf1)_0\\) come from \\(V_{0,0}\\) and the\nzero Hopf weight of \\(V_{0,1}\\).  All eight other types occur once.\nSchur's lemma therefore gives \\(M_2(\\mathbb C)\\oplus\\mathbb C^8\\).\n\\end{proof}",

      "source_as_printed": "Suppose a marked $2I$ packet is already licensed as a mathematical\nsame-owner support in the current finite stage.       "id": "BH-IIE-C-0082:INTERPRETED_COMBINED_BOUND_INVARIANCE",

        "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_369",
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c"
      },
      "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[One exact finite word presentation for all prescribed native observables]\n\\label{p2e:cor:v275-joint-observable-exactification}\nFix a supplied tetrahedral core $H$, its dense twin-word group\n$D_H$, a continuous native endpoint density $K$ of polynomial\ndegree two, a finite readout band $\\mathcal P_r$, and a finite\ncollection $\\mathscr F$ of continuous scalar action/readout\nintegrands and prescribed parameter-jet coefficients on the same\n$S^3$ comparison owner. Then there exists one positive finite\nprobability $\\nu$ supported on $D_H$ that reproduces the Haar\nintegrals of \\emph{all} these quantities exactly, including the\nmatrix-valued moments $\\int fK$ for $f\\in\\mathcal P_r$.\nAn upper bound on its node count is the real dimension of the\nspace generated by $1$, the real and imaginary parts of the\nentries of $fK$, and the real and imaginary parts of the\nspecified action coefficients. This bound depends on the\n\\emph{observable span}, not on the total spectrum of an untested\nmathematical host.\n\nIf all selected quantities are restricted polynomials of degree\nat most $L$, the rule may in addition be chosen\n$H$-bi-invariant and $N_{SU(2)}(H)$-conjugation invariant, with\nnodes remaining in $D_H$. The common rule is a mathematical\ncomparison presentation only. It does not prove the physical\noccurrence of a finite sampler or a physically covariant\nfinite-outcome instrument.\n\\end{corollary}",
      "status": "REFUTED",
      "lifecycle": "ACTIVE",
      "evidence_ids": [
        "BH-IIE-EV-B3-E1T-002",

      "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[One exact finite word presentation for all prescribed native observables]\n\\label{p2e:cor:v275-joint-observable-exactification}\nFix a supplied tetrahedral core $H$, its dense twin-word group\n$D_H$, a continuous native endpoint density $K$ of polynomial\ndegree two, a finite readout band $\\mathcal P_r$, and a finite\ncollection $\\mathscr F$ of continuous scalar action/readout\nintegrands and prescribed parameter-jet coefficients on the same\n$S^3$ comparison owner. Then there exists one positive finite\nprobability $\\nu$ supported on $D_H$ that reproduces the Haar\nintegrals of \\emph{all} these quantities exactly, including the\nmatrix-valued moments $\\int fK$ for $f\\in\\mathcal P_r$.\nAn upper bound on its node count is the real dimension of the\nspace generated by $1$, the real and imaginary parts of the\nentries of $fK$, and the real and imaginary parts of the\nspecified action coefficients. This bound depends on the\n\\emph{observable span}, not on the total spectrum of an untested\nmathematical host.\n\nIf all selected quantities are restricted polynomials of degree\nat most $L$, the rule may in addition be chosen\n$H$-bi-invariant and $N_{SU(2)}(H)$-conjugation invariant, with\nnodes remaining in $D_H$. The common rule is a mathematical\ncomparison presentation only. It does not prove the physical\noccurrence of a finite sampler or a physically covariant\nfinite-outcome instrument.\n\\end{corollary}",
      "interpreted_statement": "There exists a finite positive word rule with <=d atoms exact on the prescribed observable span, and for polynomial data there also exists a separately symmetrized finite invariant word rule without a claim that its final atom count remains<=d.",

        "statement_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Coordinate Hopf-charge steps and the superselection boundary]\n\\label{p2d:prop:coordinate-hopf-charge-steps}\nFix the oriented left-fibre representative of\nDefinition~\\ref{p2:def:finite-diagonal-spin-weight-hopf-charge} and write\n\\(Q_H:=Q_{H,L}=-2L_3^-\\).  The complexification of any equivariant\ncoordinate tuple of type \\((\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12)\\) admits components\n\\(X_{\\pm,\\alpha}\\), \\(\\alpha=1,2\\), such that\n\\[\n \\boxed{[Q_H,X_{\\pm,\\alpha}]=\\pm X_{\\pm,\\alpha},\\qquad\n P_qX_{\\pm,\\alpha}P_r=0\\quad\\text{unless }q=r\\pm1,}\n\\]\nwhere \\(P_q\\) are the spectral projectors of \\(Q_H\\) on the retained\ncarrier.  The same identities hold under every equivariant finite\ncompression.  These coordinate components preserve the diagonal central\nparity \\(\\Gamma_c\\) of Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:diagonal-center-grading}.\nThus Hopf grading and central parity impose different selection rules.\n\nIn particular, the nonzero intrinsic coordinate tuple does not lie in\n\\(\\{Q_H\\}'\\).  A Hopf-weight decomposition alone therefore does not\nestablish charge superselection for an accessible algebra containing that\ntuple.  The charge-invariant accessible algebra and dynamical stability\nrequired by Paper~IV, Corollary~\\ref{p4:cor:hopf-reeb-superselection},\nremain the appropriate additional conditions.\n\\end{proposition}",
        "proof_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe right spin-\\(\\tfrac12\\) factor of the coordinate representation has\n\\(-2L_3^-\\)-weights \\(\\pm1\\); its other spin-\\(\\tfrac12\\) factor\nsupplies the index \\(\\alpha\\).  Differentiating coordinate covariance\ngives the displayed commutator.  Multiplication on the left and right by\n\\(P_q,P_r\\) gives\n\\((q-r\\mp1)P_qX_{\\pm,\\alpha}P_r=0\\), proving the selection rule.\nAn equivariant compression projector commutes with \\(Q_H\\), so compression\npreserves the commutator exactly.  Central-evenness is the existing\ncoordinate-type calculation in Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:diagonal-center-grading}.\nIf every component commuted with \\(Q_H\\), the commutator identities would\nforce the entire tuple to vanish.  The intrinsic tuple is nonzero, giving\nthe final claim.\n\\end{proof}",

"""Claim-matched E4 finite/symbolic controls for II-E source lines 1-1274.
No source modification or theory-extension proof is performed.
"""
from itertools import product
from fractions import Fraction as Q
import json
import sympy as s
I=s.I
one=s.eye(2)
sigma=[s.Matrix([[0,1],[1,0]]),s.Matrix([[0,-I],[I,0]]),s.diag(1,-1)]
# Euclidean Hermitian gamma realization, no inherited source coefficients.
C=[s.kronecker_product(sigma[0],x) for x in sigma]+[s.kronecker_product(sigma[1],one)]
G=C[0]*C[1]*C[2]*C[3]
assert G*G==s.eye(4)
D=[I*G*c for c in C]
a,b=s.symbols('a b', real=True)
X=[a*c+b*d for c,d in zip(C,D)]
clifford_phase_controls=[]
for i in range(3):
 assert s.simplify(X[i]*X[3]-(a*a+b*b)*C[i]*C[3])==s.zeros(4)
for ai,bi in [(s.Rational(3,5),s.Rational(4,5)),(0,1),(1,0),(-1,0),(0,-1)]:
 Y=[ai*c+bi*d for c,d in zip(C,D)]
 assert all(s.simplify(Y[i]*Y[3]-C[i]*C[3])==s.zeros(4) for i in range(3))
 clifford_phase_controls.append([str(ai),str(bi)])
e=[C[i]*C[3] for i in range(3)]
basis=[s.eye(4),*e,e[0]*e[1],e[0]*e[2],e[1]*e[2],e[0]*e[1]*e[2]]
real_vectors=[s.Matrix([s.re(x) for x in v]+[s.im(x) for x in v]) for v in basis]
assert s.Matrix.hstack(*real_vectors).rank()==8
# Zero and raw-scale mutations: normalized output excluded exactly at zero.
assert all(x.subs({a:0,b:0})==s.zeros(4) for x in X)
raw_comm=s.simplify(X[0]*X[1]-X[1]*X[0])
assert raw_comm.subs({a:1,b:0}) != raw_comm.subs({a:2,b:0})
# Hermitian/null-cone attacks with nonunitary and complex shear controls.
z=s.Matrix([1,I]); K=z*z.conjugate().T
As=[s.diag(2,s.Rational(1,2)),s.Matrix([[1,1],[0,1]]),s.Matrix([[1,I],[0,1]])]
for A in As:
 assert A.det()==1
 th=A.conjugate().T.inv()
 for B in [A,th]:
  T=B*K*B.conjugate().T
  assert T.det()==0 and T.rank()==1 and s.re(s.trace(T))>0
 H=s.Matrix([[3,1+I],[1-I,4]])
 assert s.simplify(s.trace(th*H*A.inv()*A*K*A.conjugate().T)-s.trace(H*K))==0
 assert s.simplify((A*z)*(A*z).conjugate().T-A*K*A.conjugate().T)==s.zeros(2)
# Ray invariance under every tested nonzero complex scalar.
for c in [2,I,1+I,-3]:
 assert s.simplify((c*z)*(c*z).conjugate().T-c*s.conjugate(c)*K)==s.zeros(2)
# Invalid witnesses document why each is outside target hypotheses.
invalid_cone=[{'witness':'zero matrix','fails':'rank(K)=1'},
 {'witness':'diag(-1,0)','fails':'K>=0'}, {'witness':'I_2','fails':'rank(K)=1'},
 {'witness':'diag(1,0) acting matrix','fails':'det(A)=1'}]
# Exact unit Hurwitz group and adjacency realization.
H=[]
for k in range(4):
 for sign in [-1,1]:
  v=[Q(0)]*4;v[k]=Q(sign);H.append(tuple(v))
H += [tuple(Q(t,2) for t in signs) for signs in product([-1,1],repeat=4)]
H=sorted(H); assert len(H)==24
ix={x:i for i,x in enumerate(H)}
def mul(x,y):
 a,b,c,d=x;e,f,g,h=y
 return(a*e-b*f-c*g-d*h,a*f+b*e+c*h-d*g,a*g-b*h+c*e+d*f,a*h+b*g-c*f+d*e)
assert all(mul(x,y) in ix for x in H for y in H)
T=[x for x in H if x[0]==Q(1,2)]
A=s.zeros(24)
for j,q in enumerate(H):
 for t in T:A[ix[mul(t,q)],j]+=1
assert A.rank()==15 and A*s.ones(24,1)==8*s.ones(24,1)
chi2=[2*x[0] for x in H];chi3=[4*x[0]*x[0]-1 for x in H]
fixedH=sum(6+3*x+y for x,y in zip(chi2,chi3))/24
assert fixedH==6 and sum(chi2)==0 and sum(chi3)==0
# Trace normalization mutation on the same supported operator.
B=s.diag(*range(1,16));tau15=s.trace(B)/15;tau24=s.trace(B)/24
assert tau24==s.Rational(15,24)*tau15 and tau15==s.Rational(24,15)*tau24
assert tau24!=s.Rational(24,15)*tau15
# Level transport/integrality controls, both sign branches and negative/zero n.
R=s.Rational(2);hb=s.Rational(3)
for eps in [-1,1]:
 for n in [-2,0,1]:
  mu=eps*hb*n/R;mu0=R*mu
  assert eps*mu0/hb==n
assert R*s.Rational(1)/hb==s.Rational(2,3)
results={'all_assertions_passed':True,'protected_even_real_dimension':8,
 'protected_phase_controls':clifford_phase_controls,'zero_completion_normalization':'undefined, target correctly excludes',
 'raw_commutator_varies_with_magnitude':True,'celestial_SL2C_controls':len(As),
 'invalid_cone_attacks':invalid_cone,'hurwitz_adjacency_rank':A.rank(),
 'natural_H1_fixed_dimension':int(fixedH),'BM_natural_fixed_dimension':1,
 'trace_test':{'tau15':str(tau15),'tau24':str(tau24)},
 'moment_empty_fibre_ratio':'2/3','new_framework_results':False}
print(json.dumps(results,indent=2))

"""Exact exceptional-group moment/frontier controls for II-E's conditional atlas.
This is mathematical evidence only; group/role occurrence is not inferred.
"""
from itertools import product,permutations
from fractions import Fraction as F
from math import factorial
import json
from pathlib import Path
checks=[]
def ok(n,c,r):
 if not c: raise AssertionError(n)
 checks.append({'check':n,'passed':True,'result':r})

# Q(sqrt5) coordinates in the basis (1,sqrt5), represented as rational pairs.
def add(x,y): return (x[0]+y[0],x[1]+y[1])
def mul(x,y): return (x[0]*y[0]+5*x[1]*y[1],x[0]*y[1]+x[1]*y[0])
def neg(x): return (-x[0],-x[1])
def scale(x,c): return (x[0]*c,x[1]*c)
def pw(x,n):
 r=(F(1),F(0))
 for _ in range(n):r=mul(r,x)
 return r
zero=(F(0),F(0));one=(F(1),F(0));half=(F(1,2),F(0))
phi2=(F(1,4),F(1,4));invphi2=(F(-1,4),F(1,4))
T=[]
for j in range(4):
 for sign in [-1,1]:
  q=[zero]*4;q[j]=scale(one,sign);T.append(tuple(q))
T += [tuple(scale(half,v) for v in signs) for signs in product([-1,1],repeat=4)]
Is=set(T)
for per in permutations(range(4)):
 if sum(per[i]>per[j] for i in range(4) for j in range(i+1,4))%2:continue
 for signs in product([-1,1],repeat=3):
  v=[zero]+[scale(x,y) for x,y in zip([half,phi2,invphi2],signs)]
  Is.add(tuple(v[j] for j in per))
Is=sorted(Is)
ok('Icosahedral coordinate count',len(Is)==120,{'count':len(Is)})

# Even-coordinate moments of 2O are rational because the added vertices have
# exactly two nonzero coordinates of magnitude 1/sqrt2. Their odd moments
# vanish by independent sign reversals, as for the two other coordinate sets.
O_sq=[tuple(F(x[0]*x[0]+5*x[1]*x[1]) for x in q) for q in T]
for i in range(4):
 for j in range(i+1,4):
  for _ in range(4):
   q=[F(0)]*4;q[i]=q[j]=F(1,2);O_sq.append(tuple(q))
T_sq=[tuple(mul(x,x) for x in q) for q in T]
I_sq=[tuple(mul(x,x) for x in q) for q in Is]
def haar(es):
 n=sum(es)
 return F(__import__('functools').reduce(lambda a,b:a*b,(factorial(2*k)//factorial(k) for k in es),1),4**n*factorial(n+1))
def avg_ext(sq,es):
 acc=zero
 for q in sq:
  v=one
  for x,n in zip(q,es):v=mul(v,pw(x,n))
  acc=add(acc,v)
 return scale(acc,F(1,len(sq)))
def avg_rat(sq,es):return sum((__import__('functools').reduce(lambda a,b:a*b,(x**n for x,n in zip(q,es)),F(1)) for q in sq),F(0))/len(sq)
for name,sq,limit,external in [('2T',T_sq,2,True),('2O',O_sq,3,False),('2I',I_sq,5,True)]:
 count=0
 for es in product(range(limit+1),repeat=4):
  if sum(es)>limit:continue
  h=haar(es);v=avg_ext(sq,es) if external else (avg_rat(sq,es),F(0))
  ok(name+' even moment '+str(es),v==(h,F(0)),{'exponents':str(tuple(2*n for n in es)),'value':str(h)})
  count+=1
 checks.append({'check':name+' design summary','passed':True,'result':{'even_monomials':count,'odd_moments':'zero by coordinate sign symmetry','degree_strength':2*limit+1}})
for name,sq,n,external in [('2T',T_sq,3,True),('2O',O_sq,4,False),('2I',I_sq,6,True)]:
 es=(n,0,0,0);v=avg_ext(sq,es) if external else (avg_rat(sq,es),F(0));h=haar(es)
 ok(name+' first failed even moment',v!=(h,F(0)),{'finite':str(v[0]),'haar':str(h),'degree':2*n})

# Independently enumerate A5 and its five vertex stabilizers. These are the
# projective tetrahedral cores; each pair intersects in a cyclic order-three
# subgroup, whose binary lift is order six.
def parity(p):return sum(p[i]>p[j] for i in range(len(p)) for j in range(i+1,len(p)))%2
def comp(p,q):return tuple(p[q[j]] for j in range(len(p)))
def inv(p):return tuple(p.index(j) for j in range(len(p)))
A5=[p for p in permutations(range(5)) if parity(p)==0]
cores=[{p for p in A5 if p[j]==j} for j in range(5)]
sizes=[len(cores[i]&cores[j]) for i in range(5) for j in range(i+1,5)]
ok('Five projective tetrahedral cores',len(A5)==60 and all(len(c)==12 for c in cores) and sizes==[3]*10,{'A5_order':60,'cores':5,'core_orders':[12]*5,'pairwise_intersection_orders':sizes})

# Matrix presentation controls for abstract scalar torsion automorphisms.
def mm(A,B,p):return tuple(sum(A[2*i+k]*B[2*k+j] for k in range(2))%p for i in range(2) for j in range(2))
def mp(A,n,p):
 r=(1,0,0,1)
 for _ in range(n):r=mm(r,A,p)
 return r
def gen(gs,p):
 seen={(1,0,0,1)};todo=list(seen)
 while todo:
  a=todo.pop()
  for b in gs:
   c=mm(a,b,p)
   if c not in seen:seen.add(c);todo.append(c)
 return seen
for p in [3,5]:
 allm={a for a in product(range(p),repeat=4) if (a[0]*a[3]-a[1]*a[2])%p==1}
 A=(0,p-1,1,0);B=(0,p-1,1,1);minus=(p-1,0,0,p-1)
 G=gen([A,B],p)
 ok('Scalar SL2F'+str(p)+' binary triangle presentation',G==allm and mp(A,2,p)==minus and mp(B,3,p)==minus and mp(mm(A,B,p),p,p)==minus,{'order':len(G),'A_squared':'-I','B_cubed':'-I','AB_power':p,'AB_power_value':'-I'})

out={'kind':'E3-INDEPENDENT-EXACT','target_label':'p2e:thm:joint-exceptional-core-support-ledger','lineage':'Explicit exceptional quaternion coordinate moments; permutation A5 stabilizers; finite SL2 fields. No occurrence status imported.','checks_count':len(checks),'all_passed':True,'checks':checks}
Path(__file__).with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2))
print(json.dumps({'checks_count':len(checks),'all_passed':True}))

 if not c:raise AssertionError(n)
 checks.append({'check':n,'passed':True,'result':r})

R,hbar=s.symbols('R hbar',positive=True)

I=s.I;I2=s.eye(2);I4=s.eye(4)
sigma=[s.Matrix([[0,1],[1,0]]),s.Matrix([[0,-I],[I,0]]),s.diag(1,-1)]
C=[s.kronecker_product(sigma[0],p) for p in sigma]+[s.kronecker_product(sigma[1],I2)]
pairs=[(i,j) for i in range(4) for j in range(i+1,4)]
def W(q):return s.Matrix([[q[i]*(j==k)-q[j]*(i==k) for k in range(4)] for i,j in pairs])
c=s.symbols('c',real=True)
def K(q):
 q=s.Matrix(q);w=W(q);H=2*w*w.T-s.eye(6)
 out=s.zeros(15)
 out[0,0]=1;out[0,1:5]=2/s.sqrt(3)*q.T;out[1:5,0]=2/s.sqrt(3)*q
 out[1:5,1:5]=s.Rational(8,9)*I4+s.Rational(4,9)*q*q.T
 out[1:5,5:11]=4*s.sqrt(6)/9*w.T;out[5:11,1:5]=4*s.sqrt(6)/9*w
 out[5:11,5:11]=s.eye(6)+c*H
 out[11:15,11:15]=I4+sum((q[a]*C[a] for a in range(4)),s.zeros(4))
 return out
Q=[]

 for sign in [-1,1]:

dens=[K(q) for q in Q]

for a in range(4):
 X=s.simplify(s.sqrt(3)*R*sum((q[a]*k for q,k in zip(Q,dens)),s.zeros(15))/8)
 expected=s.zeros(15);expected[0,1+a]=expected[1+a,0]=R/2
 w=W([int(j==a) for j in range(4)])
 expected[1:5,5:11]=s.sqrt(2)*R/3*w.T;expected[5:11,1:5]=s.sqrt(2)*R/3*w

 ok('Exact eight-outcome native moment '+str(a),s.simplify(X-expected)==s.zeros(15),'native scalar/vector/protected edges R/2,sqrt2 R/3,sqrt3 R/4')

"""Independent exact checks of existing Paper II-E batch-1 claims.

Inputs are explicit mathematical objects, not Atlas verdicts or other agents'
outputs.  This checks algebra, finite support spectra and character data. It
does not certify physical occurrence or the upstream constructor grammar.
"""
from itertools import product, permutations, combinations
from fractions import Fraction as F
import json
import sympy as s

checks=[]
def ok(name, condition, result):
    if not bool(condition):
        raise AssertionError(name)
    checks.append({'check': name, 'passed': True, 'result': result})

I=s.I; I2=s.eye(2); I4=s.eye(4)
pauli=[s.Matrix([[0,1],[1,0]]),s.Matrix([[0,-I],[I,0]]),s.diag(1,-1)]
k0,k1,k2,k3=s.symbols('k0 k1 k2 k3',real=True)
K=k0*I2+sum((k*p for k,p in zip([k1,k2,k3],pauli)),s.zeros(2))
ok('Pauli determinant polynomial',s.expand(K.det())==k0**2-k1**2-k2**2-k3**2,'det K=k0^2-|k|^2')

# Independent real Lorentz matrices from spinor congruence; rational controls
# include one noncompact and one nondiagonal compact element.
As=[s.Matrix([[2,0],[0,s.Rational(1,2)]]),s.Matrix([[1,1+I],[0,1]]),s.Matrix([[s.Rational(3,5),s.Rational(4,5)],[-s.Rational(4,5),s.Rational(3,5)]])]
basis=[I2]+pauli; metric=s.diag(1,-1,-1,-1)
for n,A in enumerate(As):
    T=s.Matrix([[s.simplify(s.trace(B*A*C*A.conjugate().T)/2) for C in basis] for B in basis])
    ok('Lorentz congruence control '+str(n),s.simplify(T.T*metric*T)==metric and s.simplify(T.det())==1 and T[0,0]>0,{'T':str(T)})
    H=s.Matrix([[2,1-I],[1+I,3]])
    theta=A.conjugate().T.inv()
    dual=s.simplify(s.trace(theta*H*A.inv()*A*K*A.conjugate().T)/2-s.trace(H*K)/2)
    ok('Conjugate-dual trace pairing '+str(n),dual==0,'trace pairing invariant')

# Euclidean gamma matrices built from tensor products.  Even-algebra faithfulness
# is checked over R, including its pseudoscalar, rather than assumed from the
# relations alone.
C=[s.kronecker_product(pauli[0],p) for p in pauli]+[s.kronecker_product(pauli[1],I2)]
Gamma=C[0]*C[1]*C[2]*C[3]
a,b=s.symbols('alpha beta',real=True)
X=[a*c+b*I*Gamma*c for c in C]
ok('Protected Euclidean relations',all(C[i]*C[j]+C[j]*C[i]==2*(i==j)*I4 for i in range(4) for j in range(4)),'{Ca,Cb}=2 delta I')
ok('Protected two-parameter squared radius',s.simplify(sum((x*x for x in X),s.zeros(4)))==4*(a*a+b*b)*I4,'sum Xa^2=4(alpha^2+beta^2) I')
ok('Protected exact even phase cancellation',all(s.simplify(X[i]*X[3]-(a*a+b*b)*C[i]*C[3])==s.zeros(4) for i in range(3)),'Xi X4=(alpha^2+beta^2) Ci C4')
e=[C[i]*C[3] for i in range(3)]
mons=[I4]+e+[e[i]*e[j] for i in range(3) for j in range(i+1,3)]+[e[0]*e[1]*e[2]]
realcols=[s.Matrix([s.re(x) for x in list(m)]+[s.im(x) for x in list(m)]) for m in mons]
rank=s.Matrix.hstack(*realcols).rank()
ok('Represented real even algebra faithful dimension',rank==8,{'real_rank':rank,'Cl(0,3)_dimension':8})
R=s.symbols('R',positive=True)
rho=s.sqrt(3)*R/4
ok('Generated protected radius substitution',s.simplify(4*rho*rho-3*R*R/4)==0,'4 (sqrt3 R/4)^2=3R^2/4 > 0')
ok('Raw zero member',all(x.subs({a:0,b:0})==s.zeros(4) for x in X),'zero member exists; inverse normalization undefined there')

# Hurwitz support and natural left regular action, constructed in exact rationals.
qs=[]
for j in range(4):
    for sign in [-1,1]:
        q=[F(0)]*4;q[j]=F(sign);qs.append(tuple(q))
qs += [tuple(F(v,2) for v in signs) for signs in product([-1,1],repeat=4)]
qindex={q:i for i,q in enumerate(qs)}
def qm(q,r):
    a,b,c,d=q; e,f,g,h=r
    return (a*e-b*f-c*g-d*h,a*f+b*e+c*h-d*g,a*g-b*h+c*e+d*f,a*h+b*g-c*f+d*e)
def qi(q): return (q[0],-q[1],-q[2],-q[3])
ok('Hurwitz closure',len(qs)==24 and all(qm(q,r) in qindex for q in qs for r in qs),'24 exact unit quaternions closed under multiplication')
Ad=s.Matrix([[int(sum(q[t]*r[t] for t in range(4))==F(1,2)) for r in qs] for q in qs])
evals=Ad.eigenvals();ok('24-cell adjacency spectrum',evals=={8:1,4:4,0:9,-2:8,-4:2},{str(k):v for k,v in evals.items()})
# Spectral projector P0 onto the zero adjacency sector; complementary target E15.
P9=(Ad-8*s.eye(24))*(Ad-4*s.eye(24))*(Ad+2*s.eye(24))*(Ad+4*s.eye(24))/(s.Integer(-8)*(-4)*2*4)
P15=s.eye(24)-P9
ok('BM orthogonal rank split',P9*P9==P9 and P9.T==P9 and P9.rank()==9 and P15.rank()==15,{'rank_E9':9,'rank_E15':15})
reps=[]
for q in qs:
    reps.append(s.Matrix([[int(qm(q,r)==p) for r in qs] for p in qs]))
avg=sum(reps,s.zeros(24))/24
ok('Natural BM fixed subspace',s.trace(P15*avg)==1,'dim E15^(2T)=1')
ch1=[s.Integer(1)]*24
ch2=[s.Rational(2*q[0]) for q in qs]
ch3=[s.Rational(4*q[0]*q[0]-1) for q in qs]
chars=[ch1,ch2,ch3]; dims=[1,2,3]
inner=s.Matrix([[sum(x*y for x,y in zip(c,d))/24 for d in chars] for c in chars])
ok('Relevant quaternion irreducible characters',inner==s.eye(3),'1,V2,V3 pairwise orthonormal')
target_mult=[]
for char in chars:
    target_mult.append(s.simplify(sum(char[i]*s.trace(P15*reps[i]) for i in range(24))/24))
ok('Natural E15 relevant multiplicities',target_mult==[1,2,0],{'multiplicities':list(map(int,target_mult))})
source_mult=[6,3,1]
fixed=source_mult[0]
maxrank=sum(d*min(x,int(y)) for d,x,y in zip(dims,source_mult,target_mult))
homdim=sum(x*int(y) for x,y in zip(source_mult,target_mult))
ok('Natural H1/BM obstruction and sharp rank',fixed==6 and maxrank==5 and homdim==12,{'source_fixed_dim':fixed,'target_fixed_dim':1,'maximum_intertwiner_rank':maxrank,'minimum_kernel_dim':15-maxrank,'Hom_dim':homdim})
Ev=s.Matrix([[1]+[s.Rational(t) for t in q] for q in qs])
ok('Rank-five positive control',Ev.rank()==5 and P15*Ev==Ev,{'rank_evaluation':5,'image_contained_in_E15':True})
B=s.diag(*range(1,16))
ok('Supported trace scaling',s.trace(B)/24==s.Rational(15,24)*(s.trace(B)/15),'tau24(i B i*)=(15/24) tau15(B) for all B by trace invariance')

out={'kind':'E3-INDEPENDENT-EXACT','target':'Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex','source_lines':[1,1274],'input_lineage':'Source theorem objects, explicit Pauli matrices, explicit Hurwitz coordinates; no other agent proposals or atlas statuses read.','checks':checks,'checks_count':len(checks),'all_passed':all(x['passed'] for x in checks)}

"""Independent exact E4 controls for Paper2E batch2, lines1275-1957."""
from itertools import product

import json
import sympy as s
I=s.I
om=-s.Rational(1,2)+I*s.sqrt(3)/2
X=s.Matrix([[0,0,1],[1,0,0],[0,1,0]])
Z=s.diag(1,om,s.expand(om**2))
assert X**3==s.eye(3)
assert s.simplify(Z**3-s.eye(3))==s.zeros(3)
assert s.simplify(Z*X-om*X*Z)==s.zeros(3)
Ps=[s.diag(*[int(i==j) for i in range(3)]) for j in range(3)]
D1=Ps[0]-s.eye(3)/3;D2=Ps[1]-Ps[2]
C1=X+X.T;C2=-I*(X-X.T)
slice_basis=[s.eye(3),D1,D2,C1,C2]
vec=lambda M:s.Matrix(list(M))
realvec=lambda M:s.Matrix([s.re(x) for x in M]+[s.im(x) for x in M])
R=s.Matrix.hstack(*[realvec(M) for M in slice_basis])
assert R.rank()==5
outside=Ps[0]*X*Ps[2]+Ps[2]*X.T*Ps[0]
assert R.row_join(realvec(outside)).rank()==6
weyl=[X**a*Z**b for a,b in product(range(3),repeat=2)]
for j,A in enumerate(weyl):
 for k,B in enumerate(weyl):
  assert s.simplify(s.trace(A.conjugate().T*B)-(3 if j==k else 0))==0
matrixunits=[Ps[i]*X**a*Ps[j] for i,j,a in product(range(3),range(3),range(3))]
assert s.Matrix.hstack(*map(vec,matrixunits)).rank()==9
Ds=[P-s.eye(3)/3 for P in Ps]
assert s.Matrix(3,3,lambda i,j:s.trace(Ds[i]*Ds[j]))==s.eye(3)-s.ones(3)/3
roots=[Ps[0]-Ps[1],Ps[1]-Ps[2]]
assert s.Matrix(2,2,lambda i,j:s.trace(roots[i]*roots[j]))==s.Matrix([[2,-1],[-1,2]])
# Every real transport vector can be expressed with rho>=0; endpoints and zero.
polar_controls=[]
for c,d in [(0,0),(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1),(s.Rational(3,5),s.Rational(4,5))]:
 rho=s.sqrt(c*c+d*d)
 H=c*C1+d*C2
 assert H==H.conjugate().T
 if rho:
  assert s.simplify((c/rho)**2+(d/rho)**2-1)==0
 polar_controls.append([str(c),str(d),str(rho)])
# Cube link minus two antipodes is six-cycle; coordinate cyclic shift acts
# separately/free/transitively on sum+1 and sum-1 trimers.
cube=list(product([-1,1],repeat=3))
verts=[v for v in cube if abs(sum(v))==1]
adj={v:[w for w in verts if sum(x!=y for x,y in zip(v,w))==1] for v in verts}
assert len(verts)==6 and all(len(adj[v])==2 for v in verts)
for sign in [-1,1]:
 T=[v for v in verts if sum(v)==sign]
 assert len(T)==3
 v=T[0];orbit=[v,(v[1],v[2],v[0]),(v[2],v[0],v[1])]
 assert set(orbit)==set(T)
# Exact Lie-algebra commutant dimension: nullspace of commutators.
def spin(j):
 dim=int(2*j+1);ws=[j-k for k in range(dim)]
 Jz=s.diag(*ws);Jp=s.zeros(dim)
 for k,m in enumerate(ws):
  if k>0:Jp[k-1,k]=s.sqrt((j-m)*(j+m+1))
 return (Jp+Jp.T)/2,(Jp-Jp.T)/(2*I),Jz
J0=spin(s.Integer(0));Jh=spin(s.Rational(1,2));J1=spin(s.Integer(1))
def reps(sectors):
 blocks=[[],[],[],[],[],[]]
 for jl,jr in sectors:
  L=spin(jl);R=spin(jr);dl=int(2*jl+1);dr=int(2*jr+1)
  for k in range(3):
   blocks[k].append(s.kronecker_product(L[k],s.eye(dr)))
   blocks[k+3].append(s.kronecker_product(s.eye(dl),R[k]))
 return [s.diag(*b) for b in blocks]
def commdim(gens):
 n=gens[0].rows
 M=s.SparseMatrix.vstack(*[s.SparseMatrix(s.kronecker_product(s.eye(n),G)-s.kronecker_product(G.T,s.eye(n))) for G in gens])
 return n*n-M.rank()
h=s.Rational(1,2)

for jl,jr in sectors:
 for k in range(int(2*jr+1)):

assert s.expand(A1.subs(b,-a))==4*a
assert s.expand(A3.subs(b,-a))==4*a**3
# Marked zero locus imposes b+=a+d,b-=a-d: cubic is -6*a*d^2.
T=s.diag(a,a,a+d,a-d)
assert s.trace(Gamma*T)==0

for aa,dd in [(0,0),(2,0),(-1,0),(0,3),(0,-2)]:
 TT=T.subs({a:aa,d:dd});assert s.trace(Gamma*TT)==0 and s.trace(Gamma*TT**3)==0
# Union not span: I+QH is a traceless-weighted linear-zero mutation, cubic nonzero.

for n in [0,1,2,4,9]:

# Every nonzero scalar Q=tI is a pointwise common-zero control for arbitrary lambda.
t=s.symbols('t',real=True)

mode_counts={}
for m in range(7):
 value=sum((a+1)*(b+1) for a in range(2*m+1) for b in range(2*m+1-a))
 assert value==s.binomial(2*m+4,4)
 mode_counts[m]=value

 'generated_complex_matrix_algebra_dimension':9,'weyl_operators':9,'polar_controls':polar_controls,

 'fullH1_marked_commutant_complex_dimension':full_marked_dim,

 'marked_weighted_zero_locus':'RI union RQ_H','nonspan_control_A3_I_plus_QH':-6,

"""Independent exact verification of Paper II-E batch-2 mathematical exports.

The inputs are source-defined objects and explicit elementary matrices. No
Atlas verdict or other reviewer's result is consumed. Finite checks complement
the general arguments in the accompanying independent.json proposal.
"""
import sympy as s
from itertools import product
from fractions import Fraction as F
from pathlib import Path
import json

checks=[]
def check(name,condition,result):
    if not bool(condition):raise AssertionError(name)
    checks.append({'check':name,'passed':True,'result':result})
def zero(A):return s.simplify(A)==s.zeros(*A.shape)

# One exact Hurwitz/cube representative, independent of physical role labels.
cube=list(product([-1,1],repeat=3))
six=[x for x in cube if abs(sum(x))==1]
adj=s.Matrix([[int(sum(a!=b for a,b in zip(x,y))==1) for y in six] for x in six])
reach=(s.eye(6)+adj)**5
check('Nonaxial cube link is one six-cycle',len(six)==6 and all(sum(adj.row(i))==2 for i in range(6)) and all(x>0 for x in reach),{'vertices':6,'degrees':[2]*6,'connected':True})
Tp=[x for x in six if sum(x)==1];Tm=[x for x in six if sum(x)==-1]
cyc=lambda x:(x[2],x[0],x[1])
check('Both trimers have free transitive cyclic action',all({x,cyc(x),cyc(cyc(x))}==set(T) for T in [Tp,Tm] for x in T),{'trimer_sizes':[len(Tp),len(Tm)]})
def qm(q,r):
    a,b,c,d=q;e,f,g,h=r
    return(a*e-b*f-c*g-d*h,a*f+b*e+c*h-d*g,a*g-b*h+c*e+d*f,a*h+b*g-c*f+d*e)
q=(F(1,2),)*4;unit=(F(1),F(0),F(0),F(0));powers=[unit]
for _ in range(6):powers.append(qm(powers[-1],q))
check('Cyclic diagonal-stabilizer lift has order six',powers[3]==tuple(-x for x in unit) and powers[6]==unit and len(set(powers[:6]))==6,{'order':6,'cube':str(powers[3])})

# Trimer operators and complete finite Weyl basis.
I=s.I;I3=s.eye(3);omega=(-1+s.sqrt(3)*I)/2
X=s.Matrix([[0,0,1],[1,0,0],[0,1,0]])
Z=s.diag(1,omega,s.expand(omega**2))
P=[s.diag(*[int(i==j) for i in range(3)]) for j in range(3)]
D1=s.diag(s.Rational(2,3),-s.Rational(1,3),-s.Rational(1,3));D2=s.diag(0,1,-1)
C1=X+X.conjugate().T;C2=-I*(X-X.conjugate().T)
check('Trimer regular representation',X**3==I3 and X.trace()==0 and (X**2).trace()==0,{'character_at_identity':3,'character_at_nonidentity':0,'irreducible_multiplicities':[1,1,1]})
slice_basis=[I3,D1,D2,C1,C2]
realcols=[s.Matrix([s.re(x) for x in B]+[s.im(x) for x in B]) for B in slice_basis]
check('First-order Hermitian slice has real dimension five',all(B==B.conjugate().T for B in slice_basis) and s.Matrix.hstack(*realcols).rank()==5,{'dimension':5,'full_Hermitian_dimension':9})
phi=s.symbols('phi',real=True)
check('Transport polar parametrization',zero(s.expand_complex(s.exp(-I*phi)*X+s.exp(I*phi)*X**2)-s.cos(phi)*C1-s.sin(phi)*C2),'C(phi)=cos(phi) C1+sin(phi) C2')
check('Finite Weyl commutator',zero(Z*X-omega*X*Z) and zero(Z**3-I3),'ZX=omega XZ; X^3=Z^3=I')
W=[X**a*Z**b for a in range(3) for b in range(3)]
gram=s.Matrix([[s.simplify(s.trace(A.conjugate().T*B)) for B in W] for A in W])
check('Nine finite Weyl operators trace-orthogonal',gram==3*s.eye(9),{'Gram':'3 I9','complex_span_dimension':9})
Ds=[p-I3/3 for p in P]
defects=s.Matrix([[s.trace(A*B) for B in Ds] for A in Ds])
check('Centered projector defect Gram',defects==s.eye(3)-s.ones(3)/3,{'diagonal':'2/3','off_diagonal':'-1/3','rank':defects.rank()})
roots=[P[0]-P[1],P[1]-P[2]]
rootgram=s.Matrix([[s.trace(A*B) for B in roots] for A in roots])
check('A2 root-plane Gram',rootgram==s.Matrix([[2,-1],[-1,2]]),{'Gram':str(rootgram)})
units=[P[i]*X**((i-j)%3)*P[j] for i in range(3) for j in range(3)]
check('Projectors and shift generate all M3',s.Matrix.hstack(*[s.Matrix(B).reshape(9,1) for B in units]).rank()==9,'P_i X^(i-j) P_j=E_ij')

# All-m dimension proof is stars-and-bars: replace factors (a+1),(b+1) by
# two compositions each, and use one slack variable for a+b<=2m.
for m in range(8):
    dim=sum((a+1)*(b+1) for a in range(2*m+1) for b in range(2*m+1-a))
    check('Auxiliary lower-ideal dimension control m='+str(m),dim==s.binomial(2*m+4,4),{'m':m,'dimension':int(dim)})

# Full level-one action in six sectors: 1, SL, SR, vector, adjL, adjR.
# Rational sl2 raising/lowering generators avoid numerical diagonalization.
E2=s.Matrix([[0,1],[0,0]]);F2=E2.T;H2=s.diag(1,-1)
E3=s.Matrix([[0,2,0],[0,0,1],[0,0,0]])
F3=s.Matrix([[0,0,0],[1,0,0],[0,2,0]]);H3=s.diag(2,0,-2)
L=[s.diag(s.zeros(1),G,s.zeros(2),s.kronecker_product(G,s.eye(2)),J,s.zeros(3)) for G,J in [(E2,E3),(F2,F3),(H2,H3)]]
R=[s.diag(s.zeros(1),s.zeros(2),G,s.kronecker_product(s.eye(2),G),s.zeros(3),J) for G,J in [(E2,E3),(F2,F3),(H2,H3)]]
Q=-R[2];charges=list(Q.diagonal())
def centralizer_dimension(gens,diagonal=None):
    n=gens[0].rows
    variables=[(i,j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if diagonal is None or diagonal[i]==diagonal[j]]
    rows=[]
    for G in gens:
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                row=[(G[b,j] if i==a else 0)-(G[i,a] if j==b else 0) for a,b in variables]
                if any(row):rows.append(row)
    A=s.Matrix(rows)
    return len(variables)-A.rank(),len(variables),A.rank()
marked_dim,variables,rank=centralizer_dimension(L,charges)
check('Full H1 marked centralizer dimension by exact linear solve',marked_dim==12,{'unknowns_after_charge_restriction':variables,'constraint_rank':rank,'centralizer_dimension':marked_dim})
# Complete expected algebra basis, including the 2x2 multiplicity block.
neutral_trivial=[0,13] # scalar, and m_R=0 in right adjoint
algbasis=[]
for i in neutral_trivial:
    for j in neutral_trivial:
        B=s.zeros(15);B[i,j]=1;algbasis.append(B)
type_indices=[[1,2],[3],[4],[5,7],[6,8],[9,10,11],[12],[14]]
for inds in type_indices:
    B=s.zeros(15)
    for i in inds:B[i,i]=1
    algbasis.append(B)
check('Full H1 marked algebra is M2 plus eight scalar blocks',len(algbasis)==12 and all(B*G==G*B for B in algbasis for G in L+[Q]) and s.Matrix.hstack(*[B.reshape(225,1) for B in algbasis]).rank()==12,{'algebra':'M2(C) direct sum C^8','type_dimensions':[2,2,1,1,2,2,3,1,1]})
prot=[1,2,3,4]
Lprot=[G.extract(prot,prot) for G in L];Rprot=[G.extract(prot,prot) for G in R]
Qp=Q.extract(prot,prot);Gamma=s.diag(1,1,-1,-1);I4=s.eye(4)
unmarked_dim,_,_=centralizer_dimension(Lprot+Rprot)
marked_prot_dim,_,_=centralizer_dimension(Lprot,list(Qp.diagonal()))
check('Protected unmarked versus marked centralizers',unmarked_dim==2 and marked_prot_dim==3,{'Spin4_dimension':2,'SU2xU1_dimension':3})
check('Marked protected grading polynomial',Qp*Qp==s.diag(0,0,1,1) and Gamma==I4-2*Qp*Qp,'Q_H^2=P_R; Gamma=I-2 Q_H^2')
zL=s.diag(-1,-1,1,1);zR=-zL
check('Finite antipodal center actions',zL==-Gamma and zR==Gamma and zL*zR==-I4,'rho(zL)=-Gamma; rho(zR)=Gamma; rho(zc)=-I')
half=s.diag(*[s.simplify(s.exp(I*s.pi*q)) for q in Qp.diagonal()])
check('Half-turn grading does not equal infinitesimal generator',half==Gamma and Qp!=Gamma,'exp(i pi Q_H)=Gamma while Q_H != Gamma')
flip=s.diag(s.eye(2),s.Matrix([[0,1],[1,0]]))
a,bp,bm,d=s.symbols('a b_plus b_minus d',real=True)
Tp=s.diag(a,a,bm,bp) # basis has q=-1,+1 on the right
check('Unoriented Weyl flip identifies opposite right eigenvalues',zero(Tp*flip-flip*Tp) is False and zero((Tp*flip-flip*Tp).subs(bp,bm)),'flip invariance requires b_plus=b_minus')

# Independent polynomial trace evaluation in fixed eigenvalue matrices.
aa,bb,q=s.symbols('a_unmarked b_unmarked q',real=True)
U=s.diag(aa,aa,bb,bb)
f1=s.trace(Gamma*U);f3=s.trace(Gamma*U**3)
check('Unmarked weighted trace polynomials',s.expand(f1)==2*(aa-bb) and s.expand(f3)==2*(aa**3-bb**3),{'A1':str(f1),'A3':str(f3)})
check('Unmarked joint zero ideal',s.groebner([f1,f3],aa,bb).polys[0].as_expr()==aa-bb,'common zero locus a=b; traceless intersection is zero')
check('Traceless weighted traces',s.trace(Gamma*(q*Gamma))==4*q and s.trace(Gamma*(q*Gamma)**3)==4*q**3,'A1=4q; A3=4q^3')
marked1=s.trace(Gamma*Tp);marked3=s.trace(Gamma*Tp**3)
check('Marked weighted trace polynomials',marked1==2*a-bp-bm and marked3==2*a**3-bp**3-bm**3,{'A1':str(marked1),'A3':str(marked3)})
reduced=s.factor(marked3.subs({bp:a+d,bm:a-d}))
check('Marked real zero-locus factorization',reduced==-6*a*d*d,{'reduced_cubic':str(reduced),'zero_locus':'d=0 or a=0; scalar line union Hopf-charge line'})
check('Marked ordinary traceless restriction',s.trace(Tp.subs({bp:a+d,bm:a-d}))==4*a,'on zero locus ordinary tracelessness selects a=0, the Q_H line')
check('Union not linear span control',s.trace(Gamma*(I4+Qp))==0 and s.trace(Gamma*(I4+Qp)**3)!=0,'I and Q_H separately vanish, but I+Q_H has weighted cubic -6')
lam=s.symbols('lambda',positive=True)
normideal=s.groebner([2*lam-1,2*lam**3-1],lam)
check('No common nonzero charge rescaling of spinor/species normalization',normideal.polys[0].as_expr()==1,'2lambda=1 and 2lambda^3=1 have empty joint locus')
for n in range(5):
    check('Odd ordinary versus weighted trace control n='+str(n),s.trace((q*Gamma)**(2*n+1))==0 and s.trace(Gamma*(q*Gamma)**(2*n+1))==4*q**(2*n+1),{'odd_degree':2*n+1,'ordinary':0,'weighted':str(4*q**(2*n+1))})

# A nonabelian curvature span rules out replacing connection holonomy by an axis.
sigma=[s.Matrix([[0,1],[1,0]]),s.Matrix([[0,-I],[I,0]]),s.diag(1,-1)]
t=[-I*p/2 for p in sigma]
comm=[t[0]*t[1]-t[1]*t[0],t[1]*t[2]-t[2]*t[1],t[2]*t[0]-t[0]*t[2]]

out={'target':'Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex','source_lines':[1275,1957],'kind':'E3-INDEPENDENT-EXACT','inputs':'Explicit source-defined trimer shift/projectors, six Spin4 sectors, Cartan charge, and protected grading; no Atlas verdicts or other agents outputs.','checks_count':len(checks),'all_passed':True,'checks':checks}
Path(__file__).with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2))
